JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- for the death of Janardhan @ Janardhana B.L. in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners' case are as under:
2. That on 26.9.2021 at about 2.00 p.m. deceased Janardhan @ Janardhana B.L.
after having lunch and was standing on the extreme left side infront of the Hotel, on Dommasandra main road, beside Annapoorneshwari Wine Shop, Belathuru,
Bengaluru, at that time, driver of i20 car bearing registration No.KA-05-ML-7037 drove the same with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased.
Due to which, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Aaxis Hospital, Belathur Village, Whitefield main road, Bengaluru,
even after best treatment, he succumbed to the injuries on 30.9.2021.
Thereafter, post mortem was conducted and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners.
Subsequently, the petitioners have spent huge amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral, obsequies ceremonies and other incidental expenses.

3. It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 56 years, he was doing business-studio and earning Rs.50,000/- per month and contributing entire income towards the welfare of the family.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, life of the petitioners become dark, miserable and put to great financial hardship.
4. It is contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the i20 car bearing registration No.KA-05-ML-7037.
In this regard, Whitefield Traffic police have registered the case against the driver of the said vehicle in Crime No.61/2021.
As such, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
5. In response to the notice, respondent has appeared through his counsel and filed the written statement.

Sulochana vs Malleshaiah.M on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44393396/
2 6.
In the written statement, the respondent has contended that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further denied the entire averments made in the petition.

It is also contention of the respondent that, this respondent has sold the said vehicle infavour of one Adarsha on 28.3.2020 and the same day the respondent had delivered the above said vehicle and the respondent has received the delivery note from Adarsha and all the relevant documents i.e., RC card, form No.29 & 30 also handover to Adarsha, accordingly Adarsha is the owner of the said vehicle.
At the time of accident the respondent is not owner and also driver.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

7. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that, Janardhan @ Janardhana B.L. son of Lakshmi Kanthachari died due to the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicles accident that was taken place on 26.9.2021 at about 2.00 p.m., on Dommasandra Main road,
infront of Annapurneshwari Wine shop, beside hotel, Belathuru, Bengaluru City, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the i20 car bearing registration No.KA-05-ML-7037 in an actionable negligence ?

2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate ? from whom?
3) What order or award?
8.
In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.
Apart from her evidence placed the evidence of petitioner No.2 as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P15 to Ex.P18.

9. On the other hand, respondent has examined as RW1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 (b) &
Ex.R1(c).
The respondent has examined one Adharsha N. as RW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.R1(d).
Ex. R1, Ex.R1(a), Ex.R2 to Ex.R4 marked with consent by PW2.

10. Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.
11.

My findings to the above issues as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3:

3  R E A S O N S  ISSUE No.1:-
12.

It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the i20 car bearing registration No.KA-05- ML-7037, the alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, Janardhan @ Janardhana B.L. died in the said accident.
As such, the petitioners have filed this claim petition against the respondent.

13. On the other hand, the respondent though not disputed the accident and the death of Janardhan @ Janardhana B.L., but strongly disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the i20 car bearing registration No.KA-05- ML-7037.

14. On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the driver of the offending vehicle in question.
15. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 by name Sulochana examined as PW1.
In her examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of her oral evidence has relied upon the police documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.
. On going through the documents, Ex.P1- true copy of the FIS in Crime No.61/2021 of Whitefield Traffic Police Station.
Ex.P2- true copy of charge sheet, Ex.P3-true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P4-true copy of sketch, Ex.P5-true copy of inquest report, Ex
.P6-true copy P.M. report, Ex.P12- true copy of FIR, Ex.P13 true copy of complaint

On perusal of the police documents it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement, the S.H.O. of Whitefield traffic police have registered the case against the driver of i20 car bearing registration No.KA-05-ML-7037 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 337 of IPC.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against driver of the i20 car alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 & 304(A) of IPC.
18.
On the other hand, the respondent in order to substantiate his case, himself examined as RW1.

He has deposed in his evidence that the accident occurred on 26.9.2021 and the deceased died on 30.9.2021, there was no nexus between the injuries caused in the alleged accident and death of deceased.

Except making the allegations, the respondent has not placed any documents to prove that the accident has occurred not due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the i20 car bearing No.KA-05-ML-7037.
Further he has not made an effort to prove that there was no nexus between the injuries and the death of Janardhan.
Hence, the contention taken by the respondent cannot be accepted.

19. Further, PW1 & PW2 were subjected for cross-examination, but no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondent about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.

Sulochana vs Malleshaiah.M on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44393396/
4 20.
In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the i20 car vehicle bearing No.KA-05-ML-7037 and in the said accident, Janardhan @ Janardhana B.L. succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2:
21.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.
At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P7 to Ex.P9 and Ex.P11 have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.

22. Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the particulars of the petitioners mentioned in the cause title of the petition reflected that, the petitioner No.1 being the wife has lost her husband and the petitioner No.2 & 3 are children of the deceased have lost their love and affection of the deceased, who was the backbone of the family.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were dependents on the deceased during his lifetime.
23. The petitioners herein, have placed Aadhar card, which is marked at Ex.P8 to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 7.3.1967.
The accident occurred on 26.9.2021.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 54 years.

For his age, multiplier '11' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma"
Case.
24.
In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was a photographer and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
PW2 has placed receipts, photographs, CD and cash bill at Ex.P15 & Ex.P18.
But these documents does not disclose the exact income of the deceased per month.
Hence, in the absence of the definite income of the deceased, it is opt to consider the notional income as per law.
It is pertinent to note that, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2021.
By keeping in mind about the year of the accident and also notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- for the year 2021.

25 . Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Honourable Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others, " It was observed that, "While determining the Sulochana vs Malleshaiah.M on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44393396/
5 income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.

entities.text: 2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sulochana vs Malleshaiah.M on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component. "

26. Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3 rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4 th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
27.
In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, there are six persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.
Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
28. In the present case, deceased was aged about 54 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "11" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such, deceased was comes under the purview of 50-60 years, 10% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Annual income of the deceased was Rs.1,80,000/- per year.
Along with this, the future prospects of 10% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased comes to (Rs.1,80,000+18,000) = Rs.1,98,000/-.
And 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.

Thus, net loss of income comes to Rs.1,32,000/-
(Rs.1,98,000-Rs.66,000).

This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "11" which comes to Rs.14,52,000/-.
29.

Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is Sulochana vs Malleshaiah.
National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others
, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

30. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.16,500/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and also by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount of Rs.44,000/- each is awarded to the petitioner No.1 to 3 under the head loss of consortium.

Medical expenses;
31.
PW1 has stated in her evidence that at the time of treatment of deceased, she has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
She has placed medical bills at Ex.P14 to the extent of Rs.6,84,408/-.
On perusal of the medical bills Sl.No.3, 5, 7, 8, are the advance receipts and the sl.No.16 there is no seal and signature.
After deducting the said amount it comes to Rs.4,08,738/-.
Hence, the petitioner are entitled for Rs.4,08,738/- towards medical expenses.
32. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation under the following heads.

Compensation heads Compensation  Amount  Towards loss of Rs.14,52,000-00  dependency  Towards loss of Rs. 1,32,000-00  consortium  Towards loss of estate Rs. 16,500-00  Towards funeral & Rs. 16,500-00  obsequies ceremony  expenses  Medical Expenses Rs. 4,08,738-00  Total Rs.20,25,738-00 33.

Accordingly, the petitioners herein are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.20,25,738/-
(Rupees twenty lakhs twenty five thousand seven hundred and thirty eight only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in MFA No. 103557/2016, Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S.

LIABILITY:
34.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the i20 Car bearing registration No.KA-05-ML-7037 alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

35. On the other hand, the respondent has contended in his written statement that, he has sold the his vehicle infavour of one Adarsha on 28.3.2020 and on the same day, he delivered the above said vehicle and he received the delivery note from Adarsha and all the relevant documents i.e.,RC card,
form No.29 & 30 also handedover to Adarsha, accordingly Adarsha is the owner of the said vehicle.
At the time of accident, he is not owner of the vehicle and also driver.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation.
36. In order to prove his defence, respondent himself examined as RW1.
He has reiterated the averments made in the written statement.
In the cross-examination, he has admitted that at present also RC is in his name.
At the time of accident on 26.9.2021 RC was standing in his name.
37. Apart from this, respondent has examined one Adharsha as RW2.

He has deposed in his evidence that, the respondent has sold the said vehicle to him on 28.3.2020 and the same day the respondent had delivered the car to him and received the delivery note from him and also relevant documents i.e., RC, form No.29 & form No.30.
Hence, as on the date of accident, he is the owner of the said vehicle.
In the cross-examination, he has admitted that offending car still has not transferred to his name.
After purchasing the car he has not transferred the amount through bank.
On perusal of evidence RW2, though he has admitted that he is the owner of the vehicle, but not placed RC to show that he is the RC owner of the vehicle as on the date of accident.
In the cross-examination he has clearly admitted that RC was not transferred to his name.

38. At this stage it is relevant to rely the following decisions;
1) (2018) SCC 1 before Hon'ble Supreme Court of India between Naveen Kumar V/s Vijay Kumar and others.

entities.text: Naveen Kumar V/s Vijay Kumar and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 46. Wherein Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held that, "two claim petitions were filed under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, with respect to an accident taking place on 27.9.2009.
The vehicle involved in the accident was registered in the name of respondent No.1.

As per the said respondent had sold that vehicle to respondent No.2 on 12.7.2007 i.e., prior to the accident and had handed over to him the possession of the vehicle together with the relevant documents for transfer of the same.
The respondent No.2 stated that he had sold the vehicle to respondent No.3 on 18.9.2008.
The respondent No.3 inturn claimed that he had sold the vehicle to the appellant.

The tribunal having regarding to the facts that, the registration certificate of the offending vehicle continued to be Sulochana vs Malleshaiah.M on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44393396/
8 in the name of respondent No.1 and the vehicle was uninsured on the date of the accident, has awarded compensation to the claimants holding respondent No.1 jointly and severally liable together with the driver of the vehicle.

In appeal of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held that,
considering the principle underline the provisions of section 2(30) of New M.V. Act, wherein the registered owner of the vehicle despite transfering/selling his vehicle to another person continuous to be reflected in records of registering authority as owner of that vehicle, he would be treated as owner of the vehicle for the purposes of M.V. Act and would not stand absolved of his liability as owner under the said act."
2) (2011) 2 SCC 240 before Hon'ble Supreme Court of India between Pushpa @ Leela and others V/s Shakuntala and others 39. Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held that, "even though vehicle was sold out to third person but the name continued to be owner in certificate of registration then the R.C. owner is liable to pay compensation".

entities.text: Pushpa @ Leela and others V/s Shakuntala and others 39
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 40. On perusal of the citations it is clear that, "though in law, there would be a transfer of ownership of vehicle, that, by itself, would not absolve the party, in whose name the vehicle stands in RTO records, from liability to a third person.

Merely because the vehicle was transferred does not mean that the R.C.owner stands absolved of his liability to a third person, so long as his name continues in RTO records, he remains liable to a third person".

Further it is clear that, the provisions of section 2(30) of New M.V. Act, wherein the registered owner of the vehicle despite transfering/selling his vehicle to another person continuous to be reflected in records of registering authority as owner of that vehicle, he would be treated as owner of the vehicle for the purposes of M.V. Act and would not stand absolved of his liability as owner under the said act.
41.

In the instant case, it is pertinent to note that, though the respondent had sold his vehicle to RW2 on 28.3.2020 and delivered his vehicle to him and also received form No.29 & 30 from Adharsha, even though RW2 has accepted he is the owner of the said car, but in the cross-examination they have clearly admitted that RC was not transferred to RW2, it is still in the name of respondent.
Hence, it is crystal clear that as on the date of accident RC was standing in the name of the respondent.
42. In the light of decisions, the respondent cannot escape from his liability to pay the compensation as he is the owner of the vehicle in the RTO records.
43. Further, RW1 has deposed in his evidence that, at the time of incident on 29.9.2021, Adarsha and Mahantesh Marthandi were requested to him to resolve the dispute.

Hence, himself, Adarsha and Mahanthesh Marthandi were paid compensation of Rs.3,20,000/- to the deceased Janardhan B.L. for full and final settlement and the same day deceased Janardhan executed the Memorandum of settlement before the witnesses, at the time of payment of Rs.3,20,000/- petitioner No.1 & 2 were present and they were received the same.
In view of full and final settlement knowing fully well the petitioners have filed false petition against him.
They have identified their signatures which are marked at Ex.R1(b) & Ex.R1(c).
In the cross-examination he has stated that, on 27.9.2021 they met Sulochana vs Malleshaiah.

M on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44393396/
9
Janardhan in the hospital and made settlement for Rs.3,70,000/-, at that day Janardhan was taking treatment in casuality.
Further stated that Adarsha gave amount of Rs.3,70,000/- and Mahanthesh brought stamp paper.
They have not settled dispute in police station.
In Ex.R1 Janardhan sign was there.
Further admitted that sign of the Janardhan as per Ex.P1 was different when compared with Ex.R1.
Further denied the suggestion that Ex.R1 is created for the purpose of this case.

44. Added to this, RW2 has stated in his evince that, on 29.9.2021 himself and respondent have paid compensation amount of Rs.3,20,000/- to the deceased Janardhan B.L. and petitioner No.1 & 2 for full and final settlement and the same day deceased Janardhan was executed Memorandum of settlement infavour of respondent.
He has identified his signature at Ex.R1(d).
In the cross-examination has stated that he gave Rs.3,20,000/- to Sulochana and her daughter infront of one Whitefield Corporator.
To adjust the said amount, he has pledged gold.
Further he has admitted that there is no document to show that he has pledged his gold.
In Ex.R1 there is no signature of corporator and claimants.
45. Per contra, in the cross-examination, PW2 has denied that, herself and her mother received Rs.3,20,000/- from owner of the vehicle and its driver.
In Ex.R1 her father name is there.
In Ex.R1 Mallesh and Mahanthesh signatures were there.
But there is no signature of her father.
Further denied the suggestion that they have received the amount, but to get more compensation they have filed this petition.
46. On perusal of Ex.R1, it appears that the present petitioners and respondent are not parties to the said settlement deed.
Further, after accident deceased was in ICU for treatment.
His signature is disputed by the petitioners.
Under such circumstances, the burden is on the respondent to prove that, RW2 had paid Rs.3,20,000/- to the petitioners.
The cited witnesses in Ex.R1 are belonged to RW1 & RW2.
Further, respondent has not examined witnesses cited in Ex.R1 to prove the contents.
Apart from this, there is no supporting documents to prove that, Rs.3,20,000/- has been given to the petitioners, because RW2 has stated that he arranged the said amount by pledging gold.

If really,
RW2 could have raised gold loan by pledging gold ornaments, then the banker would have issued receipts in this regard.
In cross-examination, RW2 has admitted that he has no receipts or documents to show that, he pledged the gold ornaments for securing the loan.
In the absence of material documents, it is held that the respondent has failed to prove that, there was a settlement between deceased and driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
47. In the light of the above said discussion, it is held that respondent is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
48.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
 O R D E R

The claim petition filed by the Sulochana vs Malleshaiah.M on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44393396/
10 petitioners
U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.20,25,738/- (Rupees twenty lakhs twenty five thousand seven hundred and thirty eight only) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for the share of 60%, the petitioner No.2 is entitled the share of 15%, the petitioner No.3 is entitled the share of 25%.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.1 & 2, 40% of their share shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% of their share shall be released in favour of them through due process of law.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.3, entire amount shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of her choice till she attains age of majority.
After attaining the age of majority, entire amount shall be released to her through due process of law.
The guardian of the petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

4. It is contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the i20 car bearing registration No.KA-05-ML-7037.

opennyai_summary.issue:
7. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that, Janardhan @ Janardhana B.L. son of Lakshmi Kanthachari died due to the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicles accident that was taken place on 26.9.2021 at about 2.00 p.m., on Dommasandra Main road,
infront of Annapurneshwari Wine shop, beside hotel, Belathuru, Bengaluru City, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the i20 car bearing registration No.KA-05-ML-7037 in an actionable negligence ?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate ? from whom?
3) What order or award?
8.
14. On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the driver of the offending vehicle in question.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against driver of the i20 car alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 & 304(A) of IPC.
18.
Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the i20 car vehicle bearing No.KA-05-ML-7037 and in the said accident, Janardhan @ Janardhana B.L. succumbed to the injuries.
Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.
Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 7.3.1967.
But these documents does not disclose the exact income of the deceased per month.
Hence, in the absence of the definite income of the deceased, it is opt to consider the notional income as per law.
It is pertinent to note that, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2021.
By keeping in mind about the year of the accident and also notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- for the year 2021.
26. Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3 rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4 th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
27.
In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, there are six persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.
28. In the present case, deceased was aged about 54 years as on the date of the accident.
And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such, deceased was comes under the purview of 50-60 years, 10% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Annual income of the deceased was Rs.1,80,000/- per year.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation.
In appeal of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held that,
considering the principle underline the provisions of section 2(30) of New M.V. Act, wherein the registered owner of the vehicle despite transfering/selling his vehicle to another person continuous to be reflected in records of registering authority as owner of that vehicle, he would be treated as owner of the vehicle for the purposes of M.V. Act and would not stand absolved of his liability as owner under the said act."
2) (2011) 2 SCC 240 before Hon'ble Supreme Court of India between Pushpa @ Leela and others V/s Shakuntala and others 39. Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held that, "even though vehicle was sold out to third person but the name continued to be owner in certificate of registration then the R.C. owner is liable to pay compensation".
Merely because the vehicle was transferred does not mean that the R.C.owner stands absolved of his liability to a third person, so long as his name continues in RTO records, he remains liable to a third person".
Further it is clear that, the provisions of section 2(30) of New M.V. Act, wherein the registered owner of the vehicle despite transfering/selling his vehicle to another person continuous to be reflected in records of registering authority as owner of that vehicle, he would be treated as owner of the vehicle for the purposes of M.V. Act and would not stand absolved of his liability as owner under the said act.
41.
In the instant case, it is pertinent to note that, though the respondent had sold his vehicle to RW2 on 28.3.2020 and delivered his vehicle to him and also received form No.29 & 30 from Adharsha, even though RW2 has accepted he is the owner of the said car, but in the cross-examination they have clearly admitted that RC was not transferred to RW2, it is still in the name of respondent.
Hence, it is crystal clear that as on the date of accident RC was standing in the name of the respondent.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Along with this, the future prospects of 10% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased comes to (Rs.1,80,000+18,000) = Rs.1,98,000/-.
And 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
Accordingly, the petitioners herein are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.20,25,738/-
(Rupees twenty lakhs twenty five thousand seven hundred and thirty eight only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in MFA No. 103557/2016, Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S.
